scope: write the API reference the corpus gap exposed, then probe it

artifact.why: the plugin exposes 12 host routes and documented none of them as an interface — api-doc-check had nothing of ours to run on, which is how the gap surfaced

probe.method: called the real handler with 12 crafted requests before trusting any documented shape
list: backfill fields: wrote running/queued, actual status + listed/scanned/discovered/changed/truncated
bulk archive of a session with nothing pending: wrote 200 with archived: 0, actual 400 'No pending items in this session'
the two check 400s: wrote them unordered, actual order is pack lookup then boolean type
reviewProgress fields: wrote checked/total/ready, actual completed/requiredCompleted/complete/incomplete — the field a front-end reads first
pack.checks is an array on /packs but an object keyed by checkId inside an item's reviewPack — one name, two shapes
POST /sample was not documented at all, and it returns 201, the only non-200 success
probe.conclusion: six of six were shapes, not prose. Writing the document was worth less than probing it.

asserts: the four read routes and their keys
404 error shape for a missing id
unknown route never leaks a stack trace
bulk disposition refuses anything but archive, and empties 400
a real item with a real pack reaches 'checked must be a boolean'
403 on the whole prefix when connection is unavailable
every one of the 12 documented routes exists

site.fixtureFix: test/site-build.test.js had to copy docs/API.md and docs/adr/ into its temp fixture, or the build fails ENOENT — the same fixture hazard as the vertical-kit site test

observation: the corpus keeps finding what reading cannot: a check with no document to run on is a check whose gap is invisible. Both this and the previous four defects were found by asking 'what real artifact should this check be pointed at', not by reading the check.
